"Now we've got industrial scale AI going through all of this looking for vulnerabilities, probably more and deeper than all the world's hackers combined. And we're going to continue to find more and more of it."

"It underscores the idea that we can't stop. We have to move forward with AI. If the argument is going to be out of Washington, we got to slow down, China will just continue to move forward and give it to North Korea and let them unleash it on everybody else."

"But once we're through this, we will have much more robust and much safer systems."

"Markets won't anticipate this any more than it anticipates any other event. When markets have decided that these events are significant, they'll adjust."

"The ultimate example that we're all familiar with is January 2020. There was a virus coming out of China. Markets said nothing to see here and they kept going up. Around late February 2020, markets decided, okay, now there's something to see here, and they went straight down."

"If these vulnerabilities continue, we'll wake up one day and they'll be down, and they will just start to react to it until we do something about it. And that's the risk we face."

"So much of our business model in finance is based on frictions and laziness, and AI is now threatening that. They're obfuscating it by saying, I'm trying to protect you."

"The question I ask is, who are you really protecting? Are you protecting me, or are you protecting your own profits?"

Capital is now becoming the constraint…whoever can raise the most will win.

ANTHROPIC'S IPO DOCUMENTS ARE CALMING DOWN THE MARKETS.

None of the numbers released today are that different from what we heard last week, but now we know how much cash they have. 

Anthropic has $120B in cash and is likely raising $100B on the IPO. They are then likely going to be raising another $100B in debt, $60B of it already financed by BlackStone. If you assume a 3x in ARR, which probably is low considering how much the street wants them to grow, this company should have around $300-$400B in cash. This also doesn't take into account the future ATMs they might engage in.

So, the reason AI stocks are getting some relief right now is because it seems like Anthropic will have enough cash to pay their bills, which obviously is good for $NVDA, $SPCX, $AMD, $AVGO, $MU, and many other players. 

However, there are going to be 24 separate unlocks in 2027. Those are going to be days where the market has to deal with a massive amount of supply coming onto the market. The company effectively has unilateral control, not shareholders, on deciding to pause or slow down the release of models. The open-weight models continue to be a threat as more enterprises are seeing the value in owning their AI for a significantly cheaper cost. Anthropic has outlined all these risks in the S1.

Regardless on if you are buying the IPO, it seems like there is enough cash they can raise to continue paying their bills and making sure the downstream value flows into most of the semis...if the market changes their mind on that or Anthropic stalls in growth, those names get hit. But if the company keeps growing and raises cash, the money should be there to fund the semis...it's now a question on how much of a risk people want to take in actually owning the stock.

My quick takeaways on the Anthropic S-1:

1. This is a historical moment 

2. $6.6M in revenue per employee!! Hard to even comprehend how good that is but Anthropic is AI native as it gets so makes sense. 

3. I always thought OpenAI would drop their S-1 first 

4. Customers spend about 9x more after a year. Net Revenue Retention is approximately 900% as of Sep 30, 2026. Good SaaS companies brag about 120%.

5. Cowork is growing faster than Claude Code did. Goes to show you the demand for consumer products. Duo will probably rip.

6. 3 years ago this company did $41M in revenue. In the first six months of 2026, it did $16.3 billion. I don't think anyone has a mental model for that curve yet, I sure don’t. 

7. Nearly half of revenue comes through cloud marketplaces. About 48% comes from customers buying through them. Big companies buy where their budget already lives, and the lesson for founders selling to enterprises is to get listed where your buyers already spend.

8. Their run rate formula is published: the last 28 days of usage times 13, plus subscriptions times 12, which i guess is the new ARR math for founders?

9. It looks like They're merging Cowork into Claude dot au which tells you the chat box era is ending and the "go do the work for me" era is here.

10. Thousands of Anthropic employees are about to become liquid at once, so expect the biggest wave of new AI startups and angel checks San Francisco has ever seen. Reminds me when Facebook went public but this is way bigger. 

Let’s go! 

11. Buried in the filing, Anthropic says the gap between what Claude can do and how widely it's used is one of its biggest growth opportunities, so the company itself is telling you the models are ahead of the market and someone has to close that gap for dentists, landlords, and plumbers.

12. Whatever happens, exciting times to be building in AI.
